name: Axolotl
intro: An axolotl is a salamander that lives in water. It lives in lakes near Mexico City.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: An axolotl has frilly gills on its head.
Its mouth looks like it is smiling.
Most wild axolotls are brown or dark gray.
Some axolotls are pink and white.
It can grow about as long as a ruler.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Wild axolotls live only in Mexico.
They live in lakes and canals near Mexico City.
They stay in the water their whole lives.
Very few axolotls are left in the wild.
People are cleaning the canals to help them.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Axolotls eat worms and insects.
They also eat tadpoles and small fish.
They hunt for food at night.
They suck food into their mouths.
They swallow tiny stones to help mash their food.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A mother axolotl lays hundreds of eggs.
She sticks the eggs on plants or rocks.
The eggs hatch in about two weeks.
Unlike a frog, it keeps its gills when it grows up.
An axolotl can live 10 to 15 years.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: An axolotl can grow back a lost leg.
It can breathe through its skin.
It can make its skin lighter or darker to hide.
Its name comes from the name of an Aztec god.
Pet axolotls are raised by people, not taken from lakes.

vocab.meaning: An animal that can live in water and breathe air, like a frog.
An amphibian with a long tail that looks like a lizard.
Body parts that help an animal breathe under water.
When very few of an animal are left.
A long, narrow waterway made by people.
